reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that 1 at% Gd micro-alloying significantly affects glass-forming ability in Pd-Ni-P, supporting the premise that Gd can alter amorphous formation. However, the hypothesis extends this to a completely different alloy system (CrMnFeCoNiP) and claims specific mechanisms (atomic mismatch, nucleation hindrance, delayed crystallization) that are not directly evidenced in E1, leaving key mechanistic premises unsupported.
premises: Gd addition increases atomic size and chemical mismatch, enhancing chemical disorder
Increased disorder impedes heterogeneous nucleation during cooling
Increased disorder delays crystallization upon reheating
Micro-alloying with Gd significantly impacts glass-forming ability in Pd-Ni-P, unlike Co, Cu, Fe
